newsitem.title: USA: Democrats complain about fund raising probe.
newsitem.headline: Democrats complain about fund raising probe.

text.p: Democrats complained Thursday that a Senate investigation of campaign fund raising had degenerated into a "partisan street fight" because Republicans were refusing to probe their own misdeeds.

Ohio Sen. John Glenn, the ranking Democrat on the Senate Governmental Affairs Committee which is running the investigation, called a news conference to complain that the Republican majority was refusing to issue subpoenas requested by the Democrats.
"I don't view it as bipartisan now. We have been stymied at most everything we have tried to do," Glenn said. "I don't think it's fair when we're only going after one side."

The committee was investigating whether China and other foreign interests sought to influence U.S. foreign policy by helping President Clinton and the Democratic Party with illegal political contributions.

It also was investigating whether the White House or the Democrats knowingly solicited, received or laundered foreign funds. The FBI and a House committee were conducting simultaneous but separate investigations.
Flanked by four other Democratic senators, Glenn said the committee had issued 85 of 86 subpoenas requested by Republicans but only 8 of 37 requested by Democrats.

Democrats wanted to investigate a think tank established by the Republicans which received a $2 million loan guarantee from a Hong Kong company. The Republicans returned $122,000 to the company earlier this month when it learned the money came from overseas.
The Democratic Party, which is deeply in debt, has returned $1.5 million which it suspected came from foreign interests and promised to repay another $1.5 million as soon as it can afford to do so.
Much of that money came from Asian business interests or individuals who have since fled the country or who have refused to cooperate with the investigation.

While the House investigation had been sharply partisan from the outset, Tennessee Sen. Fred Thompson, the Republican who chaired the Senate committee, had promised to run a balanced probe that went after both parties.
But Connecticut Democratic Sen. Joe Lieberman said the investigation had degenerated into a "partisan street fight."

Committee spokesman Paul Clark denied that Thompson was running a one-sided investigation and charged the Democrats with trying to delay proceedings. The committee's mandate runs out at the end of this year and it was supposed to produce a final report by January 1998.
"It's delay and obfuscation. There's no intent by the Democrats to expedite this investigation," he said.
Despite their complaints, there is little the Democrats can do to challenge Thompson's running the investigation any way he wants except to try to discredit it in the eyes of the voters.
